skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Browser automation for AI agents using the inference.sh CLI. It opens remote browser sessions, uses element refs for interactions, captures screenshots or video, supports proxies, uploads files, and can execute page JavaScript.
skill.summary: Automates remote browser sessions with element refs, screenshots, video, proxies, form actions, uploads, and page JavaScript.
skill.author: 101-skills

security_audit.summary: Many static findings are markdown, example URL, relative-link, or cleanup-pattern false positives. Confirmed risk remains because the skill enables remote browser automation with external CLI commands, screenshots, video, proxies, authenticated sessions, file uploads, and page JavaScript. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent checks before recording, disable video by default for login or admin flows, and document redaction requirements for shared artifacts.

remediation.issue: Credential, TOTP, session, and cookie handling
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookie extraction examples, require secret-manager usage for credentials, and warn users not to expose session output in logs or screenshots.

remediation.issue: Proxy rotation and rate-limit avoidance guidance
remediation.suggestion: Remove rate-limit avoidance language, require authorization for proxy use, and frame proxy support around testing, corporate access, or compliance-approved scenarios.

remediation.issue: Shell templates accept arbitrary URLs and output paths
remediation.suggestion: Validate URL schemes, quote variables consistently, restrict output directories, and add warnings before file upload or execute actions.

Browser automation for AI agents via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh). Uses Playwright under the
1. **Open** - Navigate to URL, get `@e` refs for elements
| `open` | Navigate to URL, configure browser (viewport, proxy, video recording) |
| `snapshot` | Re-fetch page state with `@e` refs after DOM changes |
| `interact` | Perform actions using `@e` refs (click, fill, drag, upload, etc.) |
| `screenshot` | Take page screenshot (viewport or full page) |
| `execute` | Run JavaScript code on the page |
| `close` | Close session, returns video if recording was enabled |

semantic_findings.description: The authentication guide instructs users to fill passwords, generate TOTP codes, reuse authenticated sessions, and extract cookies. This is legitimate automation guidance, but it creates high-impact risk if used on accounts without strong data handling controls.

semantic_findings.title: Proxy Rotation and Anonymity Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The proxy guide describes rotating proxies for rate limit avoidance and privacy-focused proxy routing. This can support authorized geo-testing, but it also enables evasion of site controls and origin attribution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guide explicitly labels proxy rotation for rate limit avoidance and documents privacy proxy use. It later asks users to respect rate limits, but the evasion-capable workflow remains present.

semantic_findings.title: Arbitrary Page JavaScript and Data Extraction

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The files directly describe arbitrary in-page JavaScript execution and automated extraction of page text or links. No target authorization enforcement is shown in the skill files.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Workflows with Agent Browser
content.value_statement: AI agents often need a browser to inspect pages, submit forms, and capture visual evidence. This skill provides remote browser sessions with element refs, screenshots, video, proxies, and reusable shell workflows.
actual_capabilities: Opens remote browser sessions and returns element refs, page titles, URLs, and screenshots.
Clicks, fills, types, selects, scrolls, drags, waits, navigates, and uploads files through element refs.
Runs JavaScript in the current page and returns extracted results with screenshots.
Records WebM session videos and captures viewport or full-page screenshots.
Supports HTTP, HTTPS, and SOCKS proxy settings with optional proxy credentials.
Includes shell templates for forms, authenticated sessions, and content capture workflows.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt or infsh CLI and valid service access.
Screenshots, videos, cookies, and extracted page text may contain sensitive data.
The skill does not verify that a target site allows automation or scraping.
Element refs expire after navigation or page changes and must be refreshed.

use_cases.title: Validate Web Workflows
use_cases.description: Run browser steps, capture screenshots, and record videos for manual review or QA evidence.

use_cases.title: Extract Page Content
use_cases.description: Collect visible text, links, and structured page state from authorized websites for analysis.

use_cases.title: Prepare Product Documentation
use_cases.description: Record guided browser flows and capture key screens for tutorials or support materials.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open this URL with agent-browser, summarize the page title, visible interactive elements, and any screenshot observations.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Simple Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-browser to inspect the form, identify the current element refs, fill the approved test values, submit, and report the result.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Debugging Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Record a browser session for this authorized workflow, perform each step, close the session, and summarize the video and screenshot evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Run an Authenticated Research Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use an approved account and secret source to sign in, avoid recording sensitive screens, extract only permitted data, and close the session.

output_examples.input: Inspect a product settings page and identify the main actions.
output: Opened the page and captured a current screenshot.
Found navigation links, a search input, two toggles, and a save button.
Recommended re-snapshotting after each settings change before the next action.

output_examples.input: Submit an approved test contact form and verify completion.
output: Located the name, email, message, and submit controls from the latest snapshot.
Filled the provided test values and submitted the form.
Verified the thank-you state and captured a final screenshot.

output_examples.input: Record a failing checkout test for review.
output: Started a browser session with recording enabled after sensitive login screens were skipped.
Captured the failing interaction and saved a video reference from session close.
Reported the failed step, visible error message, and current page state.

best_practices: Use the skill only on sites and accounts where automation is authorized.
Disable recording for login, payment, admin, or personal data screens.
Re-snapshot after navigation or dynamic page changes before using element refs.
anti_patterns: Using proxies to evade rate limits, access controls, or site policies.
Recording credentials, cookies, personal data, or private admin workflows.
Running arbitrary JavaScript or uploading files without explicit approval.

faq.question: What does this skill control?
faq.answer: It controls a remote browser session through the inference.sh CLI and returns page state, screenshots, and optional video.

faq.question: Can it click and fill forms?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses snapshot element refs to click, type, fill, select, scroll, drag, and submit forms.

faq.question: Does it require another tool?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the belt or infsh CLI and access to the inference.sh agent-browser service.

faq.question: Can it record sensitive pages?
faq.answer: It can record browser sessions, so users must disable recording for credentials, personal data, and private pages.

faq.question: Does it support proxies?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents HTTP, HTTPS, and SOCKS proxy settings, including authenticated proxy credentials.

faq.question: Is it safe for unrestricted scraping?
faq.answer: No. Users must verify permission, site terms, rate limits, and data handling requirements before automation.
